# Two CloudWatch alarms have NO actions, so they fire into an empty room

## Context / Problem

`rebar-gerrit-voter-errors` is the alarm the review-bot's fail-closed path depends on:
`voter.py`'s `_voter_error()` writes a greppable `VOTER_ERROR` marker,
`infra/scripts/observability.sh` §4 publishes `rebar/host:voter_errors`, and
`infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` alarms on it. The chain is real and the metric genuinely
publishes (~22 datapoints over 2h, consistent with the 5-minute probe).

**But the alarm declares no actions, so nothing tells a human when it fires.** Verified on both
sides: `grep -nE "actions" infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` returns NOTHING, and live
`describe-alarms` returns `AlarmActions: []`, `OKActions: []`, `ActionsEnabled: true`. The alarm
transitions `OK -> ALARM` correctly and silently — discoverable only by someone already looking
in the CloudWatch console, i.e. precisely the person who does not need an alarm.

**Why it matters.** The `LLM-Review` vote gates every landing on `main` (ADR-0013). When the
voter fails closed, changes become unsubmittable — a failure that is *silent to Gerrit by
design* (no vote rather than a wrong one), and now also silent to the operator. Discovered while
working the Bedrock production cutover [rebar:eb6e-f43a-e86b-443a], whose ORDERING criterion
treats this alarm as the safety net that must be proven before the model flip.

## The defect is cited, not asserted

Two authoritative in-repo statements establish that an actionless alarm is a defect here, so this
is not merely the reporter's expectation:

1. `infra/terraform/monitoring.tf:205-207` — of a previously-adopted alarm: *"created
   out-of-band with an EMPTY alarm_actions list (so it never notified). Bringing it under IaC
   also WIRES it to the SNS topic, **closing the silent-alarm gap**."* Empty `alarm_actions` is
   named, in this repo's own IaC, as a gap to be closed.
2. `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf:19-21` — this alarm's own header states its purpose is that
   it *"surfaces a persistently broken voter to an operator instead of letting unsubmittable
   changes stack up unnoticed."* The resource does not do what its own contract says.

**Counter-evidence considered and rejected:** `monitoring_1fa8.tf:38-42` says it *"mirrors S4b's
voter_errors alarm; UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS ... because a broken CI dispatcher silently blocks
ALL submits."* That reads as if S4b's silence were deliberate — but the stated rationale for
wiring 1fa8 ("silently blocks ALL submits") is *equally* true of S4b by ADR-0013, and S4b's own
header claims operator notification. So 1fa8's author observed the omission and rationalized it
rather than fixing it; it documents the convention FROM the one instance that does not follow it.
This is a defect, not intended behavior.

## No operator decision is needed — the target is the established convention

This was queued as "needs the operator to pick a notification target". It does not. An audit of
all **13** `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` blocks in `infra/terraform/` shows **eleven** set BOTH
`alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions` to the shared `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn`:

    HAS-ACTIONS  g2p_dispatch_errors             monitoring_1fa8.tf:74-75
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_bot_merge_change_errors  monitoring_88ab.tf:62-63
    HAS-ACTIONS  deploy_errors                   monitoring_autodeploy.tf:57-58
    HAS-ACTIONS  review_interrupts               monitoring_autodeploy.tf:128-129
    HAS-ACTIONS  root_disk_pressure              monitoring_autodeploy.tf:180-181
    HAS-ACTIONS  bedrock_invoke_client_errors    monitoring_eb6e.tf:121-122
    HAS-ACTIONS  mirror_out_of_sync              monitoring_ws7.tf:52-53
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_gate_down                monitoring.tf:88-89
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_system_check                monitoring.tf:135-136
    HAS-ACTIONS  ec2_instance_check              monitoring.tf:161-162
    HAS-ACTIONS  gerrit_data_disk_high           monitoring.tf:239-240
    NO-ACTIONS   voter_errors                    monitoring_s4b.tf:35   <-- this ticket
    NO-ACTIONS   replication_errors              monitoring_s5.tf:30    <-- SIBLING

The fix is to follow the existing pattern, not to choose a target. (A prior comment recorded an
operator ruling naming `joeoakhart@navapbc.com`; that is the existing email subscription ON
`aws_sns_topic.alerts`, so wiring the shared topic satisfies it — no new destination resource.)

## SCOPE — fix BOTH alarms in this one change

`replication_errors` (`infra/terraform/monitoring_s5.tf:30`) has the IDENTICAL defect, the
identical shape, and no ticket of its own. These two are the ONLY alarms in the repo lacking
actions. Fixing one and leaving the other guarantees rediscovery later, and would mean two
terraform applies for one line each. **This ticket's scope is expanded to cover both.**

In scope:
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s4b.tf` — add `alarm_actions` + `ok_actions`.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_s5.tf` — same, for `replication_errors`.
- a new regression guard test (below).

Out of scope: `observability.sh` (the publishers are correct and working), and the alarms'
thresholds (`period = 300`, `evaluation_periods = 1`, `threshold = 0` are deliberate and fine).

## Approach

1. Add `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` and `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`
   to BOTH resources, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`. Wire OK as well as ALARM so a recovery
   is visible and the alarm does not read as stuck-firing.
2. Correct `monitoring_1fa8.tf`'s now-false "UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS" comment.

## The guard is the point, not just the two fixes

Two instances that both survived review means the convention is not checkable. Add a **test that
parses every `resource "aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm"` block under `infra/terraform/` and FAILS on
any block lacking `alarm_actions`**, so alarm number 14 cannot ship mute.

Guard requirements:
- **Anti-vacuity assertion (mandatory).** The test MUST assert the parser actually found the
  alarms — `assert len(alarms) >= 13`. A guard that silently parses zero blocks is the exact
  failure class this session has been fixing all night (bugs 34c2, 8a5e, 1909); without this the
  guard is a tautology that passes forever after any parser or layout drift.
- **Explicit opt-out, never silence.** If some future alarm legitimately should not notify, the
  guard must require a documented marker comment (e.g. `# rebar:allow-actionless-alarm: <reason>`)
  inside that resource block. Absence of actions must never pass by default.
- Offline text-contract test, following the existing precedent
  `tests/unit/test_mirror_lock_terraform.py`. New file: `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`.

## Testing

The guard is RED before the fix (it fails naming `voter_errors` and `replication_errors`) and
GREEN after — that ordering is the proof. Anti-vacuity is verified by mutation: point the parser
at an empty directory and confirm the test FAILS rather than passes.

Note the alarm wiring itself cannot be unit-tested end-to-end; live confirmation is an apply-time
observation, recorded below as a residual.

## REMEMBER THE APPLY — landing is not applying

Committing this does NOT create the notification. Applies are manual and
[rebar:1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38] records that the Terraform drift check does not gate a Gerrit change,
so un-applied infra lands and reads as done. Whoever works this MUST state explicitly whether the
change was APPLIED or merely MERGED. If no AWS credentials are available, say so plainly and
record the un-applied state as an open residual rather than implying the alarms now notify anyone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `voter_errors` (`monitoring_s4b.tf`) declares `alarm_actions` AND `ok_actions` pointing at
      `aws_sns_topic.alerts`, matching `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`.
- [x] `replication_errors` (`monitoring_s5.tf`) does the same, in the SAME change.
- [x] a guard test parses every `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` block in `infra/terraform/` and
      fails on any lacking `alarm_actions`; it was seen RED before the fix and GREEN after.
- [x] the guard carries an anti-vacuity assertion (`>= 13` alarms parsed) that itself fails when
      the parser finds nothing.
- [x] the guard requires an explicit documented opt-out marker for any intentionally silent alarm.
- [x] `monitoring_1fa8.tf`'s "UNLIKE S4b it WIRES SNS" comment is corrected.
- [x] the report and the ticket state PLAINLY whether the change is APPLIED or only MERGED. If
      only merged, the un-applied apply is recorded as an explicit open residual and the ticket
      does NOT claim the alarms notify anyone in production.
